headline: Re-cut to the spec's own gate rules, the living-update is an honest partial: only 3 of 14 countries are OECD level-validated (DK, FR, NL), and among them the paper's 'in-work transfer beats demogrant' result holds in just 1 of 3 (France; Denmark's and the Netherlands' trade-off is numerically undefined in 2026) — the widely-quoted '8 of 10' is a descriptive, OECD-unvalidated statistic.

Spain and Italy are contradicted by the benchmark (ES +34.7 vs +9.8; IT +22.9 vs -7.4, opposite sign) and are removed from the PTR-change metric.

notes: This card SUPERSEDES the 001/002/003 cards for publication (artifact-level correction). The old studies' numbers trace and are unchanged; their reporting violated the spec's validation rules (provenance audit §4–§5, §7). Old studies stay on disk untouched.
Status partial: FR and EL remain τ-unvalidated (gate-3c MTR add-on aborts on retry); the headline is an honest partial because |V| = 3 < 10.

Deviation from the instruction's provisional expectation: it anticipated V = {DK, FR} and a -14.7 pp median; because the NL gate-3 completion PASSED, V and V_Δ are {DK, FR, NL} and the conformant median is -5.2 pp. Both figures are reported.

The '8 of 10' survives only as a descriptive, unvalidated statistic; the validated-set claim is '1 of 3, France only, DK & NL undefined'. Neither softened nor inflated — the Ψ-instability (bottom-decile ≈100% traps) is itself the finding.
Full old→corrected claim map in results/card_corrections.csv; corrections to 003 in results/findings_addendum_003.md; new 1998 no-UB baseline in results/baseline_1998_noUB.csv.

Tooling only (euromod 0.4.0, .NET 8.0.31) was installed to run the 3 gate completions; no data fetched beyond the staged files and the paper PDF. Compute ~0.3 core-h (0.22 prior + this study's completions), budget < 2 core-h.
